checkpoint_name.description:
The checkpoint's CEDANA_CHECKPOINT name (the env value it restores from),
used to group automatic/named checkpoints. Null for unnamed checkpoints.

delta.description:
Whether the checkpoint is a (GPU delta) increment. Authoritative even
when parent_checkpoint_id is null (malformed id at ingest, parent deleted)

parent_checkpoint_id.description:
Checkpoint this one is an increment of; null for full checkpoints and
for deltas whose parent is unknown or deleted

workload_kind.description:
Owning workload kind of the checkpointed pod: "DynamoGraphDeployment" when
the pod belongs to a Dynamo deployment, else the pod's immediate
ownerReferences kind (ReplicaSet/Job/StatefulSet…). Null if unknown.

ActionDetails.description: Action details response for a single action

node_name.description: Node where the pod was running

reason.description: Reason for the action (heartbeat, manual, nodeTermination, etc.)

ArtifactResidency.description:
Whether an artefact can still be restored from, and why. status is only what the
control plane last recorded, which a reboot does not update.

artifact_boot_id.description: Boot id recorded when the checkpoint was taken.

boot_tied.description:
True when the storage tier ties the artefact to a single boot of a
single node (`memory`, `local`). Durable tiers survive reboots.

flags_verified.description:
Whether the engine flags still match what the next worker would start with. The
compatibility key does not cover them.

node_boot_id.description: Boot id the node is reporting now, per the latest cluster sync.

reason.description: One sentence an operator can act on, naming the evidence.

state.description:
restorable when every check in the controller's rejectArtifact passes; otherwise
the value names the check that failed.

AutoRestorePolicyInfo.description: Auto-restore policy info - represents pods/jobs with CEDANA_CHECKPOINT env var

id.description: Virtual ID based on the job/pod ID

pod_count.description: Number of pods (1 for pods, count for jobs)

created_at.description:
When this intent row was first created. Not when the request it currently
describes was made: the row is reused for a repeated ask. Use requested_at for that.

requested_at.description:
When a caller last asked for this exact state and replica count, so it orders
requests as they were made rather than as the row happened to change.

updated_at.description:
When this row last changed for any reason, including the expiry sweep. Not an
ordering key for what a caller asked for.

Checkpoint.description:
Checkpoint is basic unit for cedana service operation
it stores all the information regarding the snapshot we can use to save and then restore state

delta.description:
Whether this checkpoint is a (GPU delta) increment. Authoritative even
when parent_checkpoint_id is null (malformed id at ingest, parent deleted)

parent_checkpoint_id.description:
Checkpoint this one is an increment of; null for full checkpoints and
for deltas whose parent is unknown or deleted

last_restored_at.description: When a worker last became ready from this artefact.

observed_restore_attempts.description:
Worker pods started from this artefact, ready or not. The gap against
observed_restores is the interesting part.

observed_restores.description:
Worker pods started from this artefact that went on to serve. Counted from the
pods that ran, so it answers how many times the checkpoint was actually used.

oneOf.description:
Whether the bytes this artefact names are still there. Filled in after
the row is read (see `annotate_artifacts`); never selected from SQL.

restore_count.description:
Unmaintained; do not display. Only restore_count_increment on the artifact PATCH
writes it, and no caller sends that. Use observed_restores.

incremental.description: GPU delta (incremental) checkpoint; None = cluster default

CheckpointRequestView.description: An on-demand checkpoint request and how far it has got.

artifact_id.description: The artifact the checkpoint produced, once it succeeded.

error.description: Why it failed, in the controller's words.

kind.description: checkpoint or restart. One row per profile, so asking twice returns the open one.

request_id.description:
Identifies this attempt. A caller polling with the id it was given
cannot be shown a later request's outcome as though it were its own.

CostSavingsEstimate.description: Cost savings estimate with user-provided hourly rate

checkpoint_overhead_cost.description: Cost of checkpoint overhead (time spent checkpointing)

max_recovery_point_seconds.description: Maximum potential data loss on failure (seconds) - worst case recovery point

max_savings_per_failure.description:
Estimated maximum cost saved per failure event
(time_protected - max_recovery_point) * hourly_rate / 3600

CreateClusterRequest.description: CreateClusterRequest is the request body for creating a cluster

raw_key.description: The raw key, shown exactly once at creation.

DeploymentProgress.description: How far a profile has got, and how long each stage took.

cold_start_ms.description:
Measured activation-start-to-ready, absent until the profile is ready. A
time-to-ready, and only a cold start when start_kind is not restore.

restore_checkpoint_path.description: The checkpoint the worker was told to restore from, when it was.

start_kind.description:
How the worker behind this activation started: restore, cold, or null when no
live worker pod is known.

DeploymentStep.description: One recorded step in a profile's deployment, newest first.

elapsed_ms.description:
Milliseconds since the activation began, so a UI can draw the sequence
without doing date arithmetic. Null when the activation start is unknown.

kind.description: Lifecycle kind, e.g. model.weights_ready, model.ready, route.published.

DynamoCheckpointEntry.description:
One CEDANA_CHECKPOINT "slot" in the library. A name can have many individual
checkpoints over time (you can checkpoint the same env value repeatedly); this
aggregates them into a single slot row.

checkpoint_count.description: Number of (non-deprecated) checkpoints captured under this name

created_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent checkpoint under this name

deployment_name.description: Deployment whose CEDANA_CHECKPOINT env equals this checkpoint's name, if any.

model.description: Model served by that deployment (drives the model logo + "deploy from").

restorable.description: True if at least one checkpoint under this name is ready + restorable

DynamoCheckpointResult.description: Result of checkpointing a DGD: the workers a checkpoint was issued for.

DynamoCheckpointSummary.description: A lightweight summary of checkpoints taken for a Dynamo deployment's workers.

has_cache.description: True if at least one checkpoint with status='ready' exists

latest.description: Timestamp of the most recent checkpoint

total.description: Total number of ready checkpoints across all worker pods

DynamoCheckpointedWorker.description: One worker pod that a checkpoint was issued for.

DynamoDeployRequest.description: Request body for submitting a DynamoGraphDeployment to a cluster.

enable_checkpointing.description: If true, inject runtimeClassName: cedana and CEDANA_CHECKPOINT into worker pod specs

checkpoint_name.description:
CEDANA_CHECKPOINT name of the first worker service, if checkpointing is
enabled. This is the stable key a worker restores from. None if unset.

frontend_endpoint.description: Resolved frontend endpoint: external_ip:port or cluster_ip:port

DynamoDeploymentView.description: Combined view returned by the list endpoint

DynamoMetricPoint.description: A single metric time-series point returned to the UI.

DynamoMetricSample.description: A single metric sample sent by the watcher.

DynamoMetricsIngestRequest.description: Batch of metric samples posted by the watcher after scraping /metrics.

DynamoScrapeRequest.description: Body sent by the dynamo-watcher after scraping /v1/models from the live frontend.

pod_name.description: Pod currently using this GPU (if any)

GpuTimeSeries.description: Time-series data for a single GPU

GpuTimeSeriesPoint.description: Time-series data point for GPU metrics

le.description: Upper bound of the bucket (seconds or bytes); `null` marks the overflow bucket above the last bound.

HttpError.description:
Standard JSON error body for all 4xx/5xx responses.

Handlers return plain-text errors internally; [`normalize_error_response`]
converts anything the stack produces (handlers, extractors, the auth layer)
to this shape, so generated SDK clients can rely on a single error schema.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong

ondemand_price_per_hour.description: Hourly cost when running as on-demand

spot_price_per_hour.description: Hourly cost when running as spot

K8sResource.description: A Kubernetes resource tagged by "type", with the resource's raw JSON fields alongside the tag
K8sResource.title: K8sResource

KvCacheState.description: What a profile's engine is currently reusing.

block_size.description:
Tokens per KV block. Reuse happens in whole blocks, so a prompt shorter than two
of them reports no hits however often it repeats.

pod_name.description:
Which worker answered, so a caller can tell a restart apart from a
counter that merely moved.

queried_tokens.description: Prompt tokens the engine has looked up, cumulatively.

reused_tokens.description: Of those, how many skipped prefill because they were already resident.

LifecycleEnvelope.description: Shared envelope for trusted lifecycle events.

action_id.description: Checkpoint/restore action UUID when the event belongs to one.

activation_id.description: Model activation row UUID when applicable.

artifact_id.description: Checkpoint artifact UUID for checkpoint events.

event_id.description:
Idempotency key: generated once per logical event and reused across
transport retries (RabbitMQ redelivery, HTTP retry).

node_uid.description: Node the event came from (checkpoint tmpfs artifacts are boot-tied).

occurred_at.description: When the event happened at the source (RFC3339 UTC).

payload.description: Free-form JSON; required fields vary per kind.

schema_version.description: MUST be 1; anything else is dead-lettered on ingestion.

sequence.description: Per-(cluster_id, activation_id) monotonic counter; 0 when not applicable.

LifecycleEventView.description: One durably-persisted lifecycle event, across every profile in the cluster.

kind.description: Lifecycle kind, e.g. model.ready, route.published, route.withdrawn.

profile_id.description:
The profile the event belongs to, when known. Null for cluster-wide events
and for rows written before the column existed.

pause_ns.description: Checkpoints: time the workload was held (see facts::checkpoint_pause_ns).

pod_scheduled_at_ms.description: Restores: PodScheduled / Ready transitions of the restored pod, once known.

restores.description: For a checkpoint, every restore made from it; empty for a restore.

pod_scheduled_at_ms.description: Restores only: PodScheduled / Ready transitions of the restored pod, once known.

pause_p50_ns.description: Checkpoints: pause percentiles over attempts with a pause recorded (0 otherwise).

to_ready_p50_ns.description: Restores: PodScheduled→Ready percentiles over attempts whose pod reached Ready (0 otherwise).

OperationsSummary.description: Windowed aggregates over the same facts and bucket boundaries as the Prometheus export.

total_estimated_savings.description: Total estimated savings across all pods (spot vs on-demand)

PaginatedSlurmJobResponse.description:
One page of SLURM jobs plus the total number of jobs matching the query,
so clients can compute page counts without walking every page.

PartitionNodeCount.description: Node count per state for a partition

PipelineAction.description: Action defines WHAT to do when triggered

PipelineFilter.description: Filter defines WHAT resources are targeted

PipelinePolicyRequest.description: Request to create a policy using the pipeline format

PipelineTrigger.description: Trigger defines WHEN a policy activates

PodCheckpointCpu.description: Per-pod checkpoint resource data for efficiency calculations

checkpoint_count.description: Total number of checkpoints for this pod

cpu_at_checkpoint.description:
CPU usage (seconds) at the time of the last checkpoint
This represents the work preserved by the checkpoint

gpu_memory_used_mib.description: GPU memory used (MiB) at checkpoint time, if GPU was used

gpu_model.description: GPU model name (e.g., "NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3"), if GPU was used

gpu_utilization_at_checkpoint.description:
GPU utilization at checkpoint time (percentage 0-100), if GPU was used
Derived from DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL metric

max_recovery_point_seconds.description: Maximum interval - worst case data loss on failure (seconds)

node_name.description: Node name (for linking to node details page)

ondemand_price_per_hour.description: On-demand price per hour (from user config)

protection_efficiency_ratio.description: Ratio of time protected to checkpoint overhead (higher = more efficient)

spot_price_per_hour.description: Spot price per hour (from user config)

time_protected_seconds.description: Total time (seconds) between first and last checkpoint - time "protected"

PodStartupTime.description: Startup time for a single worker pod.

cedana_restore.description: Whether this pod was started via a Cedana restore (true) or cold-started (false)

start_time_ms.description: Time from PodScheduled → Ready in milliseconds

PodUtilization.description: Pod utilization metrics grouped by pod

oneOf.description:
An outstanding on-demand checkpoint, or null. Carried on the hosting plan the
controller already reads each pass, so it needs no extra poll.

ProfileStartupComparison.description: Cold starts against restores, for one profile.

saved_ms.description: Milliseconds a restore saves at the median.

speedup.description: Cold median divided by restore median. Above 1 means restoring is faster.

starts.description:
Every start behind the summaries, newest first, so the numbers can be
checked rather than taken on faith.

ReportWorkerEndpoint.description: Where a profile's worker publishes engine metrics (controller only).

RequestCheckpoint.description: What a caller asks for when it wants a checkpoint taken now.

reason.description:
What this checkpoint is for, carried onto the artifact so a tier holding
several has something to tell them apart by.

replace_existing.description:
Whether the previous checkpoint may be deleted to make room. On by default,
because the tier holds barely more than one dump.

pending_activation.description:
A Pending intent asks for this profile to be Active on at least one replica, so
something is trying to bring it up.

pending_intent.description:
Any capacity intent for the primary is still Pending, either direction. Rarely the
field you want; prefer pending_activation or pending_release.

pending_release.description:
A Pending intent asks for this profile to stop holding an accelerator
(Suspended, or Active at zero replicas).

restore_checkpoint_path.description: The checkpoint the live worker was told to restore from, when it was.

start_kind.description:
How the worker now on this profile started, read from the pod spec: restore when it
was given a checkpoint, cold otherwise.

service_url.description: Stable internal service URL; never contains an activation/generation.

SlurmAvailableFilters.description: Distinct filter values across all jobs (not just the current page)

SlurmCheckpoint.description:
Checkpoint is basic unit for cedana service operation
it stores all the information regarding the snapshot we can use to save and then restore state

time_suspended.description: Seconds the job spent suspended (preemption-with-checkpoint signal).

timestamp.description: Epoch seconds; falls back to start_time, then submit_time, then 0.

SlurmJob.description: SlurmJob represents a SLURM job stored in the database

derived_ec.description: Numeric derived exit code (slurmdbd derived_ec — uint32, widened to i64)

start_time.description: Unix epoch seconds; 0 means not set

submit_time.description: Unix epoch seconds; 0 means not set

SlurmJobSyncRequest.description: Sync request containing a batch of jobs

jobs.description: Raw SLURM records are retained because their schema varies by release.
